metaDescription: Six small microwaves from 0.6 to 0.9 cubic feet compared on wattage, inverter power, controls and footprint, for dorms, apartments and small kitchens.
expertTake: The LG 0.9 cu ft with Smart Inverter is the pick for 1000W and steadier reheating in a small footprint. The Commercial Chef 0.6 cu ft with mechanical dials is the value pick that has almost nothing to fail. Anyone who regularly reheats full dinner plates should skip 0.6 to 0.7 cu ft and buy a 0.9 or larger. Check wattage and plate fit before anything else. Check plate fit before price.
introParagraphs: A small microwave fits a dorm shelf, an apartment counter or an office kitchen, and it handles the everyday jobs: reheating coffee, warming leftovers and cooking frozen meals. The compromise is interior space and, often, power. Wattage and interior width are the two numbers to check. Check what you reheat most before choosing a size.

Two numbers do most of the work: the wattage that sets how fast food heats, and the interior width that decides whether a dinner plate turns freely. Controls matter too, because mechanical dials last longer while digital panels add presets. Measure your counter before you order. Presets help beginners, but dials rarely fail.

products.name: LG 0.9 Cu Ft Small Countertop Microwave, 1000W Inverter

specList.label: Exterior
specList.value: 18.75 W x 14 D x 10.69 H inches

products.description:
The LG NeoChef delivers 1000W through a Smart Inverter, which supplies steady power instead of cycling the magnetron on and off at lower settings. That matters most for defrosting and gentle reheating. It has 10 adjustable power levels, Auto Cook and a stainless finish, all in an 18.75 by 14 by 10.69 inch body.

The tradeoff is a higher price tier than the 700W models and a footprint larger than the 0.6 cu ft Commercial Chef. Compared with the Toshiba 900W, it adds 100W and the inverter. It is a premium option in the small class.

Ownership is routine. Wipe the interior after spatter, keep the vents clear and leave space around the unit. The inverter is the feature that earns the higher price. Use the lower power levels for butter, chocolate and frozen leftovers to see the benefit. If you only boil water and warm coffee, you will not notice.
products.bestFor: Small-kitchen cooks who want 1000W and smoother power control.
pros: Smart Inverter steadies power at lower settings
cons: Larger than 0.6 to 0.7 cu ft units

products.name: TOSHIBA 0.9 Cu Ft 900W Microwave
products.description:
The Toshiba lists 900W of output with a 1400W input draw, a useful reminder that wattage is the cooking power and not the plug load. It has six auto menus, a mute function and a two-step child lock. The 0.9 cu ft interior suits a standard dinner plate in most cases.

The tradeoff is that it lacks the inverter, so lower power levels cycle on and off. Compared with the LG, it gives up 100W and steady power. Against the 700W models it heats noticeably faster.

Ownership is easy. Wipe the interior, keep vents clear and use the mute function at night. The six auto menus cover popcorn, potato and similar basics, but weigh food rather than trusting presets. Check that the turntable seats before each use. It undercuts the LG on price tier while keeping a child lock.
products.bestFor: Households that want 900W in a small body with a child lock.

products.name: Chefman 0.9 Cu Ft 900W Microwave
products.description:
The Chefman 0.9 offers 900W, 10 power levels and six one-touch presets in a digital panel. The extra power levels help with melting and gentle reheating. It is a straightforward microwave.

The tradeoff is that it does not list an inverter, and the brand has less service support than LG. Compared with the Toshiba, it has more power levels but no child lock in the data. It sits in a lower price tier.

Ownership is easy. Wipe the interior and keep vents clear. With ten levels, you can drop to a low setting for melting without ruining the food. A shared kitchen benefits from simple, clearly labeled presets. It is the closest rival to the Toshiba at a lower tier.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want 900W and many power levels at a lower price tier.

products.name: COMFEE' 0.7 Cu Ft 700W Microwave with ECO Mode
products.description:
The COMFEE' has a 700W heater, a 0.7 cu ft interior, an ECO mode, a mute button and a two-step child lock. One-touch express cooking buttons simplify common tasks.

The tradeoff is that 700W is slow for full meals, and a 0.7 cu ft interior is tight for a large plate. Compared with the Toshiba 900W, it takes longer to heat the same food.

Ownership is routine. Wipe spatter and keep vents clear. Use the mute function when you cook at night. The ECO mode trims standby use, which matters if the unit sits idle most of the day. Cover food to keep the interior clean. It is a sensible bedroom or dorm choice.
products.bestFor: Dorms and bedrooms where quiet and size matter more than speed.

products.name: Commercial Chef 0.6 Cu Ft Mechanical Microwave
products.description:
The Commercial Chef is the smallest here at 17.75 by 13.44 by 9.56 inches with a 0.6 cu ft interior. Mechanical dials control time and power across six levels, and a pull handle opens the door. There is no digital panel to fail.

The tradeoff is a very small cavity, so a large dinner plate may not turn. 700W makes cooking slower. Compared with the digital models, it has no presets.

Ownership is minimal. Dials last, and wiping the interior is all it needs. Because the dials are mechanical, the timer can be off by a few seconds, so stay close for delicate jobs. It is a reliable pick for a garage or workshop. Its pull handle avoids a button latch that can wear.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants the simplest, smallest microwave with dials.
pros: Mechanical dials with little to fail

products.name: Frigidaire 0.7 Cu Ft Retro Microwave
products.description:
The Frigidaire retro microwave pairs a 0.7 cu ft cavity and 700W heater with eight one-touch auto cook menus. The retro finish suits a styled kitchen.

The tradeoff is that style adds cost and 700W is slow for full meals. Compared with the COMFEE', it has more auto menus.

Ownership is routine. Wipe the interior and keep vents clear. Choose it for a kitchen where a retro appliance is a design feature. For pure performance, a 900W model is the better buy. It matches a retro fridge or kettle.
products.bestFor: Kitchens where looks matter as much as function.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Small microwaves run 700W to 1000W. A 700W model, such as the COMFEE' or Commercial Chef, is slow for full meals. The LG at 1000W and the Toshiba and Chefman at 900W heat faster.  A 12.4 inch turntable is a good target.  For a college dorm, 700W is acceptable if you mostly heat drinks and snacks, but for dinners it adds minutes. Wattage is the number to compare.

Cubic feet is a weaker guide than turntable diameter. A 12.4 inch turntable fits a standard dinner plate. At 0.6 to 0.7 cu ft, a large plate may not turn freely.  Check the plate you use most before buying.  If a plate cannot rotate, the microwave stops or heats unevenly, so measure the widest plate you own. Plate fit decides daily use.

An inverter, as on the LG, supplies steady power at lower levels. Standard microwaves cycle the magnetron on and off. It matters most for defrosting and melting.  Defrost on low if you want even thawing.  Inverter units cost more, so reserve them for people who defrost or melt often. Check how often you defrost.

Mechanical dials like the Commercial Chef have little to fail. Digital panels add presets, as on the Toshiba and Chefman. Choose based on whether you want simplicity or convenience.  Dials suit people who dislike menus.  Dial timers can be a few seconds off, which matters little for reheating soup. Think about who will use it.

Measure the counter and leave clearance for vents. The LG is 18.75 inches wide and the Commercial Chef 17.75. Blocked vents shorten life.  Keep a few inches clear on all sides.  Leave a few inches at the back and sides so steam can leave the cabinet. Measure width, depth and height.

A child lock, as on the Toshiba and COMFEE', helps in homes with kids. A mute function helps at night.  Use the lock if kids can reach it.  Locks add safety but also add one more step to every cook. Decide if you need a lock.
